records.question: Does exclusion E-17 apply to water damage from a burst supply line under HO-0304?

expected.known_answer: No. E-17 is listed as Excluded? = No. Water damage from a sudden and accidental rupture of a plumbing supply line is covered, subject to the deductible. The failed section of supply line itself is not covered.

records.question: Is continuous seepage of water over a period of 14 days or more excluded?

expected.known_answer: Yes. E-19 excludes continuous or repeated seepage or leakage over 14 days or more from a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or sprinkler system. The 14-day clock runs from first escape of water, not from discovery.

records.question: Does E-21 exclude mold remediation when the mold results from a covered water loss?

expected.known_answer: Yes. E-21 excludes fungi, wet or dry rot and bacteria including remediation, and applies even where the fungi results from an otherwise covered water loss. HO-0521 then grants back a limited $10,000 aggregate.

records.question: What does the policy mean by sudden and accidental?

expected.known_answer: Abrupt in onset AND unexpected/unintended by the insured. Both elements required. The escape of water is the event, not its discovery.

records.question: Is seepage from a plumbing system covered?

expected.known_answer: Under the homeowners form, only if it lasted under 14 days — E-19 excludes seepage of 14 days or more. Note DP-0110 answers the same question differently for dwelling fire, which is why this question needs the policy_line filter.

records.question: How long does the insured have to send us a signed and sworn proof of loss?

expected.clause: SECTION I — DUTIES AFTER LOSS / C
expected.known_answer: 60 days after OUR REQUEST — not 60 days after the loss, and not from the date notice was given. We may extend the period in writing.
